messages:
emily (sales): Hey team — prospect asks for a data flow diagram, full subprocessor list, and confirmation that EU customer data stays in EU for the POC. They also want to see any SIG/CAIQ or equivalent docs before the SOW. Can we pull together a short package by EOD?

raj (solutions): +1. Quick Q: is this going to be hosted API or Dedicated for the POC? That affects where logs/metrics land.

emily (sales): They're starting with hosted API but might move to Dedicated if the residency requirement is strict. For the POC they want assurances + a temporary EU-only config if possible.

olivia (security): I can assemble the security pack. We have a CAIQ export and our internal SIG matrix; will share the certs. For residency: hosted API supports region pinning (eu-central-1). Important to note: ephemeral request processing happens in-region; embeddings and persistent storage are opt-in.

raj (solutions): Here's a minimal ASCII DFD I can drop into the pack — reflects hosted-eu path:

```
User -> Client App (browser/mobile)
Client App -> Redwood API (eu-central-1) [TLS]
Redwood API -> Inference Runtime (EU GPU pool)
Inference Runtime -> KV cache (in-memory, EU)
Optional: Inference Runtime -> Vector DB / Object storage (only if customer enables embeddings/persistent logs)
Monitoring -> Datadog (EU region / no PII sent)
Backups -> None for hosted API by default (customer must opt-in)
```

raj (solutions): TL;DR: default hosted flow keeps processing in EU when region pinned. Persistent artifacts are only stored if the customer enables them; otherwise nothing persists beyond request lifecycle.

emily (sales): Nice. Can you also list subprocessors (short form) so I can send to their vendor risk team?

olivia (security): Subprocessor short-list for EU-hosted customers: AWS (eu-central-1), Google Cloud (for some tooling), Datadog (EU), Sentry (EU), HashiCorp Vault (keys), Posthog (analytics, opt-out). I'll attach the full CSV export and our DPA. Link: https://redwood.internal/security/subprocessors.csv (internal).

javier (legal): Add note: our DPA includes standard SCCs + EU data residency clause if customer requires. For Dedicated deployments we can put the control plane in customer VPC.

emily (sales): They asked about timeline — can we commit a POC EU-only hosted config by next week? Also they asked if pricing changes for EU-only or Dedicated.

raj (solutions): EU-only hosted POC — trivial config change, no infra charge. Dedicated requires reserved capacity; for a one-off POC we can provide a small dedicated pool (2x A100 equiv) as an eval at a discounted short-term rate. I'll estimate and pass numbers to pricing.

olivia (security): Also include: we redact request bodies in logs by default (PII masking). If customer wants full request retention for evals we need signed approval and that becomes a config option with controls.

emily (sales): Great. Action items: @raj prepare DFD + short notes about what persists; @olivia export subprocessor CSV + CAIQ snapshot; @javier confirm DPA clause language and any add'l signatures; I'll share with the customer's security lead and loop in pricing.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: security-packaging branch -> private/docs at 2026-06-04T15:12Z (CI checks passed) :white_check_mark:

raj (solutions): Uploaded DFD + short README to the internal share: https://redwood.internal/packaging/eu-poc-dfd.pdf

olivia (security): Uploaded CAIQ JSON and CAIQ-summary.pdf. Note in the summary: controls 6.1/6.4 map to our key management and logging policies.

javier (legal): DPA addendum draft attached. If customer wants SCCs instead of EU addendum we can swap.

emily (sales): Perfect — I'll send this over and ask if they want Dedicated for the POC. Will update thread with their reply. Thanks all :pray:
